titulo: Why did they keep a propeller in a cage?
tema: The electric fan, seen by a stickman from the far future
perguntaCentral: If a fan does not make the air any colder, why did people in hot rooms feel so much better in front of one?

reliquia.descricao: an ordinary white pedestal fan from the 2020s, with three blades inside a round cage and a row of speed buttons, found in the Old Layers of planet Lumen

cenas.acao: Kip lifts a dusty pedestal fan out of a dig pit in Lumen, flicks a blade and watches it spin inside the cage.
cenas.narracao: We dug this out of the Old Layers: a *propeller* locked inside a cage. It can't fly anywhere. So what was it for?
cenas.visual: Future city, cool off-white. Kip at the edge of a dig pit holding the dusty fan up by its pole in his right hand. At 'propeller' a magnifier circle on the blades; at 'cage' the grille lines glow; at 'fly' a dashed arrow up with a red cross. He flicks a blade and it spins slowly. Two Lumen citizens shrug at 'what'.

cenas.acao: Kip taps the Chrono-Band, a ring portal opens, he steps through and arrives in a hot 2020s living room.
cenas.narracao: So I tapped my *Chrono-Band* and jumped back to the old days, the 2020s, right into a very hot summer afternoon.
cenas.visual: Kip taps his left wrist with his right hand at 'tapped'; cyan and violet ring portal opens; he walks in at 'jumped' and it collapses into a dot. Hard switch to a warm present-day living room at 'old days'; a shrinking violet ring drops him off. At 'hot' a wall thermometer reads 34° and heat shimmer rises.

cenas.acao: A sweaty present-day person presses a fan button, sits in front of the spinning blades and relaxes while Kip watches.
cenas.narracao: Back then, people in hot rooms pressed a button, sat right in front of the *spinning blades*, and sighed with relief.
cenas.visual: Living room, warm palette. PP-02 fans themself with a hand, sweat drops. At 'pressed' a finger taps the speed button and the fan starts; blades blur at 'spinning blades'; breeze lines flow over PP-02, who smiles and leans back at 'relief'. Kip watches from the left, curious.

cenas.acao: Kip holds a thermometer in the breeze and it does not move; a close-up of skin shows the breeze sweeping away warm air and sweat drops evaporating.
cenas.narracao: But the room never got cooler. The breeze swept warm air off the skin, so *sweat evaporated* faster and carried heat away.
cenas.visual: Kip holds a thermometer in front of the fan at 'never': the reading stays at 34°. Circle wipe into a skin close-up: a warm orange layer of air sits on the skin; breeze arrows sweep it away at 'swept'; sweat drops shrink into rising vapour at 'evaporated'; red heat arrows leave the skin at 'heat away'.

cenas.acao: Split screen: on top the fan blows at an empty chair and the thermometer stays put; below, on Lumen, a small cool breeze follows Kip as he walks.
cenas.narracao: Point it at an empty chair, and it cooled *nobody*. On Lumen, a cool breeze follows me around. Back then, people chased the breeze.
cenas.visual: Top half (old days): the fan blows at an empty chair; thermometer unchanged; a grey 'x' at 'nobody'. Bottom half (my time) revealed at 'Lumen': Kip walks while a small floating cyan breeze swirl follows him at 'follows'. Top again at 'chased': PP-02 drags a chair back in front of the fan.

cenas.acao: Back in the Lumen museum, Kip sets the fan in a glowing display case; a light panel shows a breeze crossing a stick figure, not a room.
cenas.narracao: So it wasn't a broken flying machine. It never cooled the air. It cooled *people*, one breeze at a time.
cenas.visual: Kip arrives from a shrinking violet ring in the museum and sets the fan in a display case. At 'air' a floating light panel shows a room thermometer with no change; at 'people' the panel switches to breeze lines crossing a little stick figure who smiles. Ends happy, holding a calm frame.
